summaries: • A2ZINFRA (Insider Trades): A2ZINFRA Engineering Limited has re-appointed Mr. Amit Mittal as its Managing Director cum CEO for a three-year term effective January 1, 2027, ensuring continuity of experienced leadership (35+ years in infrastructure) to drive strategic direction and growth. • ABDL (SAST): Executive Summary: Bina Kishore Chhabria, a promoter of Allied Blenders and Distillers Limited (ABDL), divested 5.5 million equity shares, representing 1.97% of the company's total paid-up capital, through an open market sale on September 23, 2026. This transaction reduced her individual holding from 58.20% to 56.23% and the overall promoter group's stake from 80.91% to 78.94%. While promoter selling is noteworthy, the promoter group retains a very significant majority ownership, indicating continued strong control and no immediate red flags regarding company stability or strategic direction. └ 📄 Source

• ACUTAAS (Regulatory Risk): Acutaas Chemicals Limited announced the re-appointment of Mr. Ram Mohan Lokhande as Whole Time Director and Mrs. Anita Bandyopadhyay as an Independent Director, both for a five-year tenure starting February 2027. • ADVENTHTL (Management Change): Executive Summary: Advent Hotels International Limited announced the resignation of Independent Director Mr. Rajeev RA, effective September 25, 2026. This resignation was necessitated by an RBI circular restricting NBFCs from granting facilities to companies with common directors, as Mr. RA held directorships in both Advent Hotels and Authum Investment & Infrastructure Limited, an NBFC from which Advent is seeking a financial loan. This action, while addressing a regulatory compliance issue, highlights Advent's reliance on this specific financing and required a structural change to facilitate the loan. └ 📄 Source

• BHARATCOAL (SAST): Executive Summary: Bharat Coking Coal Limited (BCCL) has been fined a cumulative ₹37.35 Lakhs by both the NSE and BSE for repeated non-compliance with SEBI LODR Regulations concerning the composition of its Board and key committees (Audit, Nomination & Remuneration, Stakeholder Relationship) for the quarters ended March and June 2026. This recurring failure to appoint requisite independent directors, including a woman director, presents a significant governance red flag, indicating systemic issues despite BCCL's assertion that appointments are beyond its direct control due to government processes. The company's board has decided to request a waiver of the fines and continue pursuing the matter with the Ministry of Coal. └ 📄 Source
